notices: Source: binbaz.org.sa (موقع الشيخ ابن باز). Site footer notice: جميع الحقوق محفوظة والنقل متاح لكل مسلم بشرط ذكر المصدر.
Reuse basis: user_confirmed_permission. The user reports email permission from the Ibn Baz website; it was not independently inspected by the importer. Attribution to the source page is required.
Arabic only: the fatwa pages link no official translation of the same fatwa; translations are empty and nothing is machine-translated.

Text is the page text: HTML entities decoded (U+00A0 kept), source-markup whitespace (newlines, tabs, indentation) collapsed to one space inside a paragraph and removed at paragraph edges,
stored as a newline. span.aaya -> quran, span.hadith -> hadith, strong/b -> strong; everything else is text. Scripts, styles, iframes, images, attributes and links are dropped.

Footnotes: each item of the page's footnote list (section.footnotes li#footnote-N) is stored in notes as {id: N, runs} in source order, one note per item, never merged; an inline marker linked to an existing note (a[rel=footnote][href=#footnote-N]) is a noteref run whose text is the marker exactly as shown (for example [1]); a marker without a note stays plain text and is reported by the validator; a note without a marker is kept unreferenced. The audio player is ignored.
Some pages draw honorifics with private-use characters (for example U+F055, U+F049, U+F074, U+F079 inside span.arabisque) that need the site's own icon font; they are kept unchanged as source text.
review_status source_preserved: ingestion checks only, no human, scholarly or language review by Balligh.

records.audience_reason: Explains that a Muslim who neglects some duties has weaker faith: faith rises with obedience and falls with sin.
records.title: التكاسل عن أداء بعض الواجبات

records.audience_reason: Answers a common curiosity: what angels, jinn and Adam were created from, citing the hadith in Sahih Muslim.
records.title: مم خلق الله الملائكة وإبليس؟

records.audience_reason: Defines what a 'religion' is and how Islam differs from other religions; basic framing for someone exploring Islam.
records.title: التعريف بالدين

records.audience_reason: Explains how major sins weaken faith without taking a Muslim out of Islam; corrects a common misconception.

records.audience_reason: Explains saying 'I am a believer, in sha Allah' and that it is not doubt; a frequent beginner question.

records.audience_reason: Explains the meaning and requirements of the first pillar (the shahada); foundational for a new Muslim.

records.audience_reason: Answers whether saying and believing the shahada is enough to enter Islam and what is expected after it.
records.title: هل يكفي النطق بالشهادتين والاعتقاد للدخول في الإسلام؟

records.audience_reason: Background to a Quran verse readers ask about (Harut and Marut, Al-Baqarah 102); secondary, not a first-step topic.
records.title: هل هاروت وماروت ملكان أو بشران؟

records.audience_reason: Explains that the basis of faith is one while people differ in its strength.
records.title: حقيقة أصل الإيمان وتفاوت الناس فيه

records.audience_reason: Gives the minimum owed to God: do the obligations and avoid the prohibitions; a clear starting point.
records.title: ما الحد الأدنى للقيام بواجب العبادة لله تعالى؟

records.audience_reason: Explains that belief in the heart alone is not enough without prayer and other deeds.
records.title: حكم الاكتفاء بإيمان القلب دون العمل

records.audience_reason: Clarifies that the shahada brings a person into Islam and why prayer then matters.
records.title: حكم من يترك ركناً من أركان الإسلام

records.audience_reason: States the two conditions of accepted deeds and Islam: sincerity to God and following the Prophet.
records.title: ما شروط الإسلام؟

records.audience_reason: Short note that the praised strength of a believer is strength in deeds, not body.
records.title: ما القوة المحمودة في المؤمن؟

records.audience_reason: Explains the meaning of the two testimonies, through which a person enters Islam.
records.title: معنى الشهادتين

records.audience_reason: Explains that a Muslim who commits a major sin is sinful but remains a Muslim (the Sunni position).
records.title: حكم مرتكب الكبيرة عند أهل السنة وغيرهم

records.audience_reason: Explains the fitrah every child is born upon; relevant to someone exploring Islam.

records.audience_reason: Defines Islam: submitting to God with tawhid and obeying Him; an ideal opening entry.

records.audience_reason: Practical guidance on how to learn and live tawhid in belief, conduct and deeds.

records.audience_reason: Lists the conditions of 'la ilaha illa Allah' and that its meaning must be understood, not only said.

records.audience_reason: Gives the Quranic evidence for the word of tawhid and what tawhid means.

records.title: كيف يتحقق التوحيد ومعنى الشرك والظلم

records.audience_reason: Explains why worshipping God alone, not only affirming Him as Lord, is the message of the prophets.

records.audience_reason: Explains an often-quoted hadith ('I was commanded to fight people...') in context; for a teacher answering questions about it, not a first step.

records.audience_reason: Discusses atheists who deny God and tawhid of lordship; relevant to someone from a non-religious background.

records.audience_reason: Corrects a common error of explaining 'la ilaha illa Allah' as only 'no creator but God'.

records.audience_reason: Addresses the phrase 'loyalty to the homeland'; secondary topic kept for teachers.

records.title: كيفية البراءة من الكافرين ودعوتهم إلى الله

records.audience_reason: Love and dislike are for a person's deeds, never for race, colour or lineage.

selection.rationale: Curated for a new Muslim or someone exploring Islam, and a teacher helping them (G4-A-P1 N10). The G4-A set was read record by record: the leaving-prayer consequence cluster was cut to three representative items, exact duplicates and advanced or personal-case rulings were replaced, and practical basics were added from official binbaz.org.sa category listings (wudu, ghusl, tayammum, prayer times, recitation in prayer, fasting intention, dutifulness to parents). Every record is fetched from its full detail URL and kept only when the full question, answer and notes pass the completeness checks; source text is never rewritten. Each index entry carries an English audience_reason.
